exercise.name: Cable Seated Face Pull (with rope)

reference.title: Cable Seated Face Pull (with rope)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

secondaryBodyParts: Upper back (middle and lower trapezius, rhomboids)
equipment: Cable machine (pulley at about eye level)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the rope to the face, breathe in as the arms reach back.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short hold, about 2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: light enough to keep the elbows high and reach the face every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; longer hold at the face

cues.text: Sit tall on a box facing the cable, feet flat; set the pulley at about eye level and hold the rope ends palms facing each other, arms long toward the pulley.
Breathe out and pull the rope toward your face, elbows travelling out and back at about shoulder height.
Hands beside the face, thumbs pointing back as the shoulders rotate out; squeeze the shoulder blades together, ribs down.
Breathe in and let the arms reach back toward the pulley under control.
Brief pause with the arms long, trunk still on the seat, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows dropping so it turns into a row
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows at about shoulder height and pull to the face, not the chest.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk still; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck long and the shoulders down while the blades draw together.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the stack snap the arms forward
mistakes.fix: Control the return over about 2 s.

kinematics.setup: Arms reaching to the pulley, ≈98° of elevation
kinematics.peak: ≈91° of elevation, elbow 1 cm vs the shoulder joint
kinematics.norm: Elbows at about shoulder height at the finish (clinical opinion; the face pull is a high, wide pull)

kinematics.setup: Upper arm ≈85° in front of the frontal plane
kinematics.peak: Upper arm ≈16° in front of the frontal plane
kinematics.norm: From the arms reaching forward to the upper arms in line with the shoulders or a little behind; prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007)

kinematics.setup: Forearm in line with the cable (≈76° from vertical)
kinematics.peak: Forearm ≈49° from vertical, hands beside the face
kinematics.norm: The shoulders turn out at the end so the forearms point up (clinical opinion); external rotation work loads the infraspinatus (Sung 2023 compared positions and abduction angles)
From nearly straight to about 90 degrees or a little more at the finish (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pulley 127.6 cm high, 115 cm in front of the shoulders; 44 cm between the hands
kinematics.peak: Grip width unchanged (43.46-44.31 cm); cable clear of the face by 13.27 cm or more
kinematics.norm: Pulley at about eye level; the rope ends stay about shoulder width apart (clinical opinion); the cable keeps the load nearly constant through the pull

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms long
kinematics.peak: 1.2 s pull, 0.5 s hold, 2 s back
kinematics.norm: About 1 s pull, 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Seated Face Pull (with rope), video (movement reference)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the shoulder or neck, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the face with the elbows high.
Keep the face out of the cable's path: the rope ends stop beside, not at, the face.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the turn-out: finish with the hands at chin height and less rotation.
Neck tension: set the pulley a little lower, at chest height.
regressions: Rear-delt row with the elbows lower.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back and out (horizontal abduction). Prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the finish; in prone retraction exercises the middle trapezius reached up to about 77% of maximal activity with the arms raised (Oyama 2010).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Turns the shoulder out at the end so the forearms point up; external rotation work loads it (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the elbows up at shoulder height.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbows as the hands come to the face.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder blade; shrugging shifts work here.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright so the body does not lean back.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back and out (horizontal abduction). Prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the finish; in prone retraction exercises the middle trapezius reached up to about 77% of maximal activity with the arms raised (Oyama 2010).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Turns the shoulder out at the end so the forearms point up; external rotation work loads it (Sung 2023).
